newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to easier.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to easier.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended steady to easier in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The interbank rate slipped further today but there was still little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were easier but bond prices were steady to easier. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.07/2.02 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.10/2.05 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.63/1.58 percent against 1.65/1.60 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.26/99.31 versus Monday's close of S$99.27/99.32.
September 2001 was unchanged from Monday's close of S$99.28/99.33 and June 2003 unchanged at S$98.85/98.90.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent versus Monday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
